## Two separate failures last night

**1. Power outage (physical, ~21:25 PDT Sep 12).** Your first "knocked itself offline" was your home power cutting out — it took down Vado *and* the JetKVM at the same instant (which is what tipped me off it wasn't software, since the KVM is on separate power). Your mom confirmed it. Vado auto-booted on its own (the Restore-on-AC-Power = Power On setting held) and rejoined the tailnet at 22:09. Nothing for me to fix there.

**2. The "Secret Sentinel" issue (self-inflicted).** While running unattended and working on itself, OpenClaw poisoned its own z.ai credential. Every model call started failing with `Secret sentinel … is not registered in this process; refusing provider runtime auth exchange`, which knocked out the main session, subagents, and heartbeat.

## Root cause

A self-session doing vault/secret experimentation mangled the z.ai credential three ways at once:
- Created a saved auth profile (`zai:manual`) whose stored "key" was actually a **write-only vault sentinel** — a value only valid for the process that minted it, so the next gateway process rejected it. That dead profile also outranked the real config.
- Stripped the `models.providers.zai.apiKey` SecretRef out of the config.
- Deleted `ZAI_API_KEY` from the vault entirely.

Collateral: it had also dropped `models.providers.ollama`, silently breaking Ollama web search.

## What I fixed (native tooling only, no custom code)

- Removed the poisoned `zai:manual` profile (had to force-stop the gateway to release the auth-store lock, then pop it out of the state DB).
- Restored the `zai` SecretRef, and re-seeded `ZAI_API_KEY` into the vault from the one place it survived — Honcho's `.env` — with allow-host `api.z.ai`.
- `secrets reload` → gateway logged **`Secret resolution recovered`** at 03:38:29 PDT. **Zero sentinel errors since.**
- Restored the `ollama` SecretRef → web search working again.
- Removed the dead `utility` container (finishing the qwen-0.6B teardown you'd asked for; the embedding model Honcho needs stays).

**Verified live:** inference E2E returned my test string; web search returned a real kernel version; `secrets audit` clean (0 plaintext, 0 unresolved); Cloudflare remote access up (`openclaw.bennettvernon.com` → 200); Honcho stack + embed all healthy.

## One thing to know going forward

This wasn't a bug in OpenClaw so much as **OpenClaw editing its own live credentials** during self-work. It can happen again any time a self-session does secret/vault work on a subscription provider's auth. The durable fix is behavioral — keep self-sessions away from rewriting the live provider credentials — rather than a watchdog (per your native-only rule). - The part that makes it genuinely useful: **scheduled automations can update pinned widgets headlessly** — an agent turn running on a cron can refresh a dashboard card with `pin: true` even when no browser or app is open. So a "morning brief" or "server health" card can stay current on its own.
